prompt: How do I insert an automatic table of contents in Word?
completion:
Below is a quick‑start guide that works in almost every modern version of Microsoft Word (2007, 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019, Office 365, etc.).  
It covers the **automatic** (dynamic) Table of Contents (TOC) that updates automatically whenever you change your document.

---

## 1.  Make sure you use the built‑in heading styles

Word builds the TOC from styles, not from the text itself.  
If you haven’t already, apply the standard heading styles (`Heading 1`, `Heading 2`, `Heading 3`, …) to the text that you want to appear in the TOC.

| Style | Typical use |
|-------|-------------|
| Heading 1 | Chapter titles, main sections |
| Heading 2 | Sub‑sections |
| Heading 3 | Sub‑sub‑sections (optional) |

**How to apply a style**

1. Highlight the text you want to include.  
2. On the **Home** tab, in the **Styles** group, click the desired heading style.  
   - To make a style look different, right‑click the style and choose **Modify**.

> **Tip:** If you need more depth, create a custom heading style (`Heading 4`, etc.) and assign it a `Outline level` of 4 or more.

---

## 2.  Insert the TOC

1. **Place the cursor** where you want the Table of Contents (usually right after the title page or at the very start of the document).  
2. Go to the **References** tab.  
3. In the **Table of Contents** group, click **Table of Contents**.  
4. Pick a built‑in style (e.g., “Automatic Table 1” or “Automatic Table 2”).  

> *If you’re on Word for Mac, the steps are identical—just the menu layout looks a bit different.*

Once you click a style, Word inserts a TOC that reflects the current heading hierarchy.

---

## 3.  Update the TOC automatically

The TOC is **not static**.  It only updates when you ask it to.  
- **Automatic update** after saving: In Word 2016/2019/365, the TOC updates automatically when you *close* the document, but you may still need to update it manually while editing.

### Manual update
- Click anywhere inside the TOC.  
- A light gray bar appears above the TOC: **Update Table** (or right‑click the TOC and choose **Update Field**).  
- Choose **Update page numbers only** or **Update entire table** (pick the latter when you add/remove headings).

### Shortcut
- **Alt + F9** toggles field codes (shows `{ TOC … }`).  
- **F9** updates the selected field (including the TOC).

---

## 4.  Customize the TOC (optional)

1. **Insert → Table of Contents → Custom Table of Contents…**  
2. In the dialog, you can:

   - **Show levels** – how many heading levels to include.  
   - **Formats** – change the numbering style or use a different tab leader (e.g., dotted lines).  
   - **Options** – map custom styles to outline levels (useful if you created a “Custom Heading” style).  
   - **Tab leader** – choose solid, dotted, or dashed lines between heading text and page number.  
   - **Modify** – click to change font, indentation, etc.

3. Click **OK**. Word updates the TOC accordingly.

---

## 5.  Common pitfalls & fixes

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| TOC shows “(no entries)” | Make sure headings use the **Heading** styles. |
| Page numbers are wrong | Click **Update Table → Update entire table**. |
| Heading text doesn’t appear | Check that the style’s **Outline level** matches the TOC depth. |
| TOC doesn’t update after printing a page break | Update manually with **F9**. |

---

## 6.  Quick‑reference cheat sheet

| Action | Shortcut | Where |
|--------|----------|-------|
| Apply Heading 1 | **Ctrl + Alt + 1** | Home tab |
| Apply Heading 2 | **Ctrl + Alt + 2** | Home tab |
| Apply Heading 3 | **Ctrl + Alt + 3** | Home tab |
| Insert TOC | **Alt + N, T** (in recent Word) | References tab |
| Update TOC | **F9** | After clicking inside the TOC |
| Toggle field codes | **Alt + F9** | Any field |

---

## 7.  Recap

1. **Style** your headings (`Heading 1`, `Heading 2`, …).  
2. **Insert** the TOC from the **References** tab.  
3. **Update** it whenever you add or delete headings.  
4. **Customize** if you need more control.

That’s it! Your Table of Contents will stay in sync with the rest of your document, saving you time and effort every time you edit. Happy writing!
